children: OpenAI
CEO
Sam Altman

said on Saturday he is "very uncomfortable" with efforts to elevate artificial intelligence into something akin to a deity. He also argued that treating models as a substitute for human decision-making creates its own kind of safety risk.
Altman Calls it a ‘Real Safety Issue’

Altman made the remarks in a post on X that reported concerns about people "trying to ascribe religious force or a surrender of human judgment to AI models." He added that he thinks that "it is a real safety issue."
I am very uncomfortable about people trying to ascribe religious force or a surrender of human judgment to AI models, and think it is a real safety issue.
Anthropic’s Outreach
The comments came days after a New York Times report detailed
Anthropic
‘s private meetings with religious scholars to discuss questions surrounding AI consciousness, morality and how Claude should behave.
According to the report, Anthropic cofounder
Chris Olah

held private sessions with religious figures and raised questions about how advanced systems should develop values as they become more capable and independent. "How do you help them be stable? How do you help them to mature? How do you help them be, you know, deeply moral?" Olah told the Times.
